Wheat.why: Wheat thrives in the Wheatbelt due to its temperate climate and well-drained soils.
Wheat.irrigation_system: Dryland farming; relies mostly on rainfall.
Wheat.grazing: Post-harvest grazing of stubble is common.
Wheat.suitability: Primarily an agricultural crop; not suitable for viticulture or horticulture.

Barley.why: Barley is well-suited to the region's climate and is a good rotational crop with wheat.
Barley.irrigation_system: Dryland farming with supplemental irrigation if needed.
Barley.grazing: Can be grazed during early growth stages.
Barley.suitability: Agricultural crop; not suitable for viticulture or horticulture.

Canola.why: Canola adapts well to the Wheatbelt and provides valuable crop rotation benefits.
Canola.irrigation_system: Dryland; ensure soil moisture at planting.
Canola.grazing: Not recommended due to potential toxicity.
Canola.suitability: Oilseed crop; not suitable for viticulture or horticulture.

Lentils.why: Lentils fix nitrogen in the soil and are suitable for the Wheatbelt's conditions.
Lentils.grazing: Can be grazed lightly before flowering.

Sunflower.why: Sunflowers are drought-tolerant and perform well in the Wheatbelt's climate.
Sunflower.grazing: Stalks can be grazed after harvest.
Sunflower.suitability: Oilseed and confectionery uses; not suitable for viticulture or horticulture.

Chickpeas.why: Chickpeas are suitable for the region and help improve soil nitrogen levels.
Chickpeas.grazing: Not recommended; plants are sensitive to grazing damage.
Chickpeas.suitability: Agricultural crop with high protein content.

Crop Rotation.why: Crop rotation enhances soil health and reduces pest and disease cycles.
Crop Rotation.irrigation_system: Depends on the specific crops used.
Crop Rotation.grazing: Can be integrated with livestock grazing systems.
